questions.stem: Which AWS storage service is a distributed object store with a flat bucket+key namespace?
questions.explanation: S3 is the canonical object store: flat namespace, key-addressed, accessed via HTTPS API.

questions.stem: Amazon S3 is designed for what durability?
questions.explanation: S3 advertises 11 nines of durability by storing data across at least 3 AZs within a Region.

questions.stem: After December 2020, S3 provides what consistency model?
questions.explanation: S3 now provides strong read-after-write consistency by default for all operations.

questions.stem: A bucket has versioning enabled. A client DELETEs an object without specifying a version ID. What happens?
choices: A delete marker is added; previous versions remain retrievable by version ID
questions.explanation: Without a version ID, S3 adds a delete marker. The object is hidden from default reads but versions can still be fetched explicitly.

questions.stem: Which storage class is cheapest for data accessed perhaps once a year that may take 12+ hours to retrieve?
questions.explanation: Deep Archive is the cheapest at-rest tier, with retrieval typically 12-48 hours.

questions.stem: Which storage class stores data in only a SINGLE AZ?
questions.explanation: One Zone-IA is single-AZ, trading availability for ~20% lower cost than Standard-IA.

questions.stem: What does S3 Cross-Region Replication require?
choices: Versioning enabled on both source AND destination
An EC2 instance acting as relay
questions.explanation: CRR requires versioning on both buckets and an IAM role granting replication permissions.

questions.stem: By default, when an object is deleted in a source bucket, what happens to the destination bucket in CRR?
choices: The delete marker is NOT replicated by default
questions.explanation: Delete markers are not replicated unless you explicitly enable delete-marker replication.

questions.stem: EBS volumes have which key locality constraint?
choices: Region-scoped, attachable to any instance in the Region
AZ-scoped, attachable only within their Availability Zone
questions.explanation: An EBS volume lives in one AZ and can only attach to instances in that AZ; to move it, snapshot and copy.

questions.stem: EC2 Instance Store is best described as:
choices: Object storage local to the host
questions.explanation: Instance store is on the host's local disks — fastest but wiped on stop or terminate.

questions.stem: Which service provides a managed POSIX file system accessible from many EC2 instances simultaneously over NFSv4.1?
questions.explanation: EFS is the multi-attach NFS service. EBS gp3/io2 are normally single-attach block volumes.

questions.stem: Which EBS volume type is the modern general-purpose SSD default?
questions.explanation: gp3 is the current default general-purpose SSD, offering baseline IOPS independent of size.

questions.stem: A bucket policy uses the condition `aws:SecureTransport: true`. What does this enforce?
questions.explanation: `aws:SecureTransport` ensures requests arrive over TLS — encryption in transit.

questions.stem: SSE-KMS differs from SSE-S3 because:
choices: SSE-KMS uses customer-managed (or AWS-managed) KMS keys with auditable usage
SSE-KMS encrypts in transit, not at rest
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS gives you key control and CloudTrail logging of key usage; SSE-S3 uses opaque AWS-managed keys.

questions.stem: What is the correct virtual-hosted-style URL for an object `pic.jpg` in bucket `acme` in `ap-southeast-2`?
questions.explanation: Virtual-hosted style puts the bucket as a subdomain: `<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<key>`.

questions.stem: An S3 lifecycle rule should transition objects to Standard-IA after how many days minimum?
questions.explanation: Standard-IA has a 30-day minimum storage duration before transition or deletion charges; transitioning earlier is not cost-effective.

questions.stem: Which AWS feature would you use to serve S3-hosted content with low global latency?
questions.explanation: CloudFront is the CDN; it caches S3 content at edge locations close to users.

questions.stem: Which storage class auto-moves objects between tiers based on access patterns?
questions.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering monitors access and moves objects between frequent/infrequent/archive tiers automatically.

questions.stem: S3 bucket names must be:
choices: Globally unique across all AWS accounts
Any name; only keys must be unique
questions.explanation: Bucket names live in a global DNS-style namespace; once taken, no other account can use the same name.

questions.stem: Which is the BEST choice for an HPC scratch filesystem requiring sub-millisecond latency and hundreds of GB/s throughput?
questions.explanation: FSx for Lustre is purpose-built for HPC scratch workloads with extreme throughput.

questions.stem: EBS snapshots are stored where?
questions.explanation: Snapshots are stored in S3 behind the scenes; you don't see them as objects in your buckets, but they inherit S3's durability.

questions.stem: An object key looks like `photos/2026/cat.jpg`. In S3, what is `photos/2026/`?
choices: A prefix; S3 has a flat namespace
questions.explanation: S3 is flat; slashes in keys are just characters. Console UIs render prefixes as folders, but no real hierarchy exists.

questions.stem: Which event source CANNOT be triggered by an S3 object upload?
questions.explanation: S3 Event Notifications target Lambda, SNS, SQS, or EventBridge — not arbitrary EC2 lifecycle actions.

questions.stem: Block Public Access on a bucket overrides what?
choices: Bucket policies and ACLs that would otherwise grant public access
questions.explanation: Block Public Access is a guard rail that overrides bucket policies and ACLs which would otherwise expose the bucket publicly.

questions.stem: Why might durability (11 nines) be higher than availability (4 nines) for S3 Standard?
choices: Durability counts data loss; availability counts ability to serve a request at any instant
Availability is per-AZ, durability is per-Region
questions.explanation: Durability = will data still exist? Availability = can I reach it now? A network outage hurts availability but data is still safe.
